title: ee.daemon.start.v1
description: Payload schema for the `data` object emitted by `ee daemon start` (see src/cli/mod.rs::handle_daemon_hot_mode_start). The outer envelope is the canonical `ee.response.v2` success envelope; this schema describes the inner `data` object only. The handler binds the Unix-domain socket and either reports the socket path and detaches (default) or blocks until terminated (`--foreground`). The schema is intentionally narrow because the SRR1 skeleton (bd-oja31) makes a small set of declarations; future slices (true daemonize, readiness poll, lifecycle PID file) may add fields under a `v2` schema rather than mutating `v1`. The skeleton's `std::mem::forget(handle)` leak (tracked in bd-37o8k) does NOT change the wire shape — the envelope still describes what the CLI claimed at emission time.

socketPath.description: Absolute path to the Unix-domain socket the daemon bound. On Linux this defaults to `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/ee/daemon.sock`; on macOS it defaults to `/tmp/ee-daemon.sock` (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not standard on Darwin). May be overridden via the `--socket` flag. Rendered via `Path::display()`, so on Windows targets the value would use backslashes — but `ee daemon start` is currently Unix-only and emits a `DomainError::Configuration` on Windows, so consumers can treat this as a POSIX path.

foreground.description: Echo of the `--foreground` flag. When `true` the CLI process blocks after emitting this envelope and the accept loop runs in the same process; when `false` the handle is leaked so the accept thread outlives the call but the parent CLI process returns. The bd-37o8k follow-up replaces the detached path with a real daemonize step (fork + setsid) and a readiness probe.
